title: A low-cost, novel endoscopic repeated-access port for small animal research
author: Ingram, Robbins, et al.

steps.title: Print and prepare ABS molds
steps.instruction: Design a two‑part mold with alignment collars in SolidWorks, export to a Parasolid file and 3D‑print the mold halves in ABS filament using a MakerBot Replicator 2X (or later produce durable aluminum molds via CNC machining).

steps.title: Sand mold surfaces
steps.instruction: Smooth the printed ABS mold halves by sanding: start with coarse‑grit sandpaper, progress to finer grits, and use small files for hard‑to‑reach areas; sand‑blasting may be used as an alternative.

steps.title: Vapor‑polish molds and rest
steps.instruction: Boil acetone in a glass reservoir, channel the vapor through a chemically‑resistant hose onto the sanded mold surfaces until a glossy finish is achieved, avoiding excessive exposure that can cause pinholes or brittleness; allow the polished molds to rest for at least 48 h to let residual acetone evaporate.

steps.title: Mix silicone elastomer
steps.instruction: Weigh Part A of Applied Silicone LSR 40 – 10:1 A:B (Implant Grade, Part #40,082, also MED‑4244) into a mixing container that is roughly ten times the expected silicone volume; add Part B equal to 10 % of the weight of Part A; mix thoroughly, minimizing but not eliminating air bubbles.

steps.title: Degas silicone mixture
steps.instruction: Place the mixed silicone in a vacuum chamber, pull the pressure down to about 29 inHg, hold for 3–5 min, then release; repeat the vacuum cycle until most bubbles are collapsed, being careful not to exceed the manufacturer’s working time to avoid premature curing.

steps.title: Assemble molds with alignment collars
steps.instruction: Insert each ABS mold half into its corresponding alignment collar; lay a polyethylene sheet (20 mm wide, 0.254 mm thick) across one half to form the future slit; interlock the collars and push the two mold halves together so they are sealed.

steps.title: Fill molds with silicone and degas
steps.instruction: Pour the degassed silicone into each assembled mold, overfilling to guarantee complete cavity fill; then place the closed molds back into the vacuum chamber and repeat the degassing cycle (≈29 inHg, 3–5 min) to remove any bubbles introduced during pouring.

steps.title: Cure silicone‑filled molds
steps.instruction: Warm the sealed molds in an oven at 66 °C for 2–3 h; increase the cure time if a larger batch of molds is being processed. (Note: some silicone formulations may not require heat; follow the silicone supplier’s instructions.)

steps.title: Demold and finish silicone port
steps.instruction: Remove the cured molds from the oven, detach them from the alignment collars, and split the mold halves to expose the silicone port; trim excess silicone and pull out the polyethylene strip from the slit, leaving a clean, self‑sealing device ready for sterilization.

steps.title: Sterilize the completed port
steps.instruction: Soak the finished port in a chlorhexidine solution, then rinse thoroughly with sterile saline, or alternatively sterilize by ethylene‑oxide gas according to institutional protocols.

steps.title: Implant port into hen
steps.instruction: Anesthetize the hen with isoflurane induction at 5 % and maintenance at 2.5–3 %; remove feathers and clean the skin with betadine followed by alcohol; make a 1.5–2.5 cm incision on the left side of the body wall caudal to the last rib; place the sterilized port so one sealing cap contacts the skin and the other lies inside the cavity; suture the port to the body wall using 2‑0 polydioxanone (PDS); recover the animal, administer buprenorphine 1 mg/kg IM and carprofen 3 mg/kg for analgesia; after 12 h evaluate the hen for signs of pain or distress.

steps.title: Perform repeated laparoscopic access
steps.instruction: Re‑anesthetize the hen using the same isoflurane protocol; insert a 4 mm rigid laparoscope (Portoscope.com) lubricated with sterile ointment through the implanted port; conduct visualization, biopsy, or chemotherapeutic delivery as needed without creating capnoperitoneum; the entire access procedure takes less than 1 min and can be performed by a single operator.
